intended_object: An internal proof interface (per the docstring and module doc): a pair made of a ZMod 2-valued linear functional on H₁(RPⁿ; F₂) and a proof that it is invariant under the homology pushforward of every map RPⁿ → RPⁿ induced by an odd self-map of Sⁿ. The library uses it as input when it builds the degree-one class α ∈ H¹(RPⁿ; F₂).
explanation:
The docstring calls this structure "the interface used to construct the degree-one class", and the module doc says it "isolates the homology functional and its invariance property". So it is data bundled for the library's own proof. The library only uses it as the input to `rpAlpha`, and through `m.invariant` it gets the naturality lemma `inducedOnRPPullback_rpAlpha`.

It is not a standard mathematical object. Nothing in the structure says the functional is the monodromy character of the double cover Sⁿ → RPⁿ. For example, the zero functional satisfies the invariance condition trivially. That canonical choice is supplied separately, by `RPnMonodromyFunctional`. Mathlib has nothing comparable to cite.
